provenance.model-knowledge: Assistant knowledge of the Bangladesh technology employer landscape; unverified against a live page.

companies.name: Samsung R&D Institute Bangladesh
companies.note: Multinational R&D centre. Hardest hiring bar in the country and the strongest pay for graduates.

companies.name: Therap (BD) Ltd.
companies.note: US healthcare product engineering built in Dhaka. Long-running graduate intake and top-quartile fresher pay.

companies.name: Brain Station 23
companies.note: Largest Bangladeshi software firm. 250-999 staff per Clutch, structured internship and trainee tracks.

companies.name: bKash Limited
companies.note: Dominant mobile financial service. Large in-house engineering group and competitive pay.

companies.name: Grameenphone
companies.note: Telenor-affiliated market leader. Well known graduate and internship programmes with transparent pay bands.

companies.name: Robi Axiata Limited
companies.note: Second largest operator. Runs graduate and digital programmes; solid pay for early-career staff.

companies.name: Banglalink Digital Communications
companies.note: VEON operator with a named graduate programme.

companies.name: Optimizely Bangladesh
companies.note: Product engineering for a global SaaS platform. Strong engineering practice and pay.

companies.name: Cefalo Bangladesh Ltd.
companies.note: Norwegian-owned development centre. Reputation for engineering culture and above-market pay.

companies.name: Enosis Solutions
companies.note: US-facing engineering services, 250-999 staff per Clutch. Hires graduates in volume.

companies.name: Dynamic Solution Innovators
companies.note: 250-999 staff, 25-49 USD per hour per Clutch. Established graduate pipeline.

companies.name: REVE Systems
companies.note: Telecom and messaging products, 250-999 staff per Clutch.

companies.name: Riseup Labs
companies.note: Games and applications, 250-999 staff per Clutch.

companies.name: Itransition Bangladesh
companies.note: Global outsourcing group with a Dhaka presence, 1000-9999 staff per Clutch.

companies.name: Musemind
companies.note: Design agency, 50-249 staff, 50-99 USD per hour per Clutch. Good for UI/UX portfolios.

companies.name: Devxhub
companies.note: Rajshahi-based, 50-249 staff per Clutch. One of the few rated firms outside Dhaka.

companies.name: ZAAG Systems
companies.note: 10-49 staff per Clutch. Small shop; verify pay and hours before committing.

companies.name: VISER X
companies.note: 50-249 staff per Clutch.

companies.name: Augmex Technologies
companies.note: 10-49 staff per Clutch.

companies.name: Genesys Softwares
companies.note: 50-249 staff per Clutch; rate not published.

companies.name: Kaz Software
companies.note: Long-established boutique with a strong engineering reputation.

companies.name: SELISE
companies.note: Swiss-owned engineering services with a Dhaka delivery centre.

companies.name: Vivasoft Limited
companies.note: Mid-size services firm that hires juniors.

companies.name: Nascenia Limited
companies.note: Ruby and web engineering shop with an internship track.

companies.name: Pathao
companies.note: Consumer superapp with real in-house product engineering.

companies.name: ShopUp

companies.name: notiionhive
companies.note: Small Uttara digital agency that runs a paid trainee track. The stated stipend is well below Dhaka developer market rate, so treat it as a learning position.

companies.name: DNationSoft
companies.note: Small Khulna software house. It states pay openly, which is unusual and welcome, but there is little public engineering evidence. Verify working hours before committing.

companies.name: GenAILabs
companies.note: Small remote-first AI outfit with little verifiable public record. The work sounds like real product engineering, but no pay is disclosed; confirm the contract and payment terms before starting.

companies.name: Ruvix Tech
companies.note: Small technology outfit with a thin public footprint. The internship offers mentorship but names no stipend; establish whether it is paid before committing time.

companies.name: GeoVision
companies.note: Surveillance and security systems integrator in Uttara. Leave and festival bonus terms are spelled out, but pay is deferred to the interview. The work is hardware support rather than software engineering.

companies.name: Ding
companies.note: International mobile top-up platform with an established engineering and IT operations presence. A reasonable first employer, though this circular discloses no pay.

companies.name: Kranti Robotics
companies.note: Robotics and automation outfit with Canadian association, running a structured internship. The stipend is stated but small, so weigh it as training rather than income.

companies.name: GFGG IT Solutions
companies.note: Small Salesforce consultancy running a paid intern track with senior-consultant mentoring. It confirms the internship is paid but not how much; ask for the figure in writing.

companies.name: PEN Group
companies.note: Chattogram-based group hiring React and AI developers. Its circulars print a salary heading and then leave it empty, and the shift ends at 10pm; confirm both before accepting.

companies.name: Dessein LAB
companies.note: Small Sylhet software house. Working hours, weekend and bonus terms are spelled out clearly, but the salary is only described as negotiable.

companies.name: AdZoic
companies.note: Dhaka adtech with unusually specific, engineering-literate circulars, which is a good sign about the technical bar. Most of its openings ask for two or more years, so only the QA role is near fresher range, and no pay is disclosed.

companies.name: Rajshahi Colo
companies.note: Regional data centre and colocation provider in Rajshahi. Genuinely open to coursework instead of experience, which is rare, but it discloses no pay and has a small public footprint.

companies.name: Web Xpress
companies.note: Small Dhaka web and mobile agency offering internships. No stipend is named, so confirm whether the position is paid before starting.

companies.name: CUBE LIMITED
companies.note: Small Mymensingh software house running a Laravel internship with no educational barrier, which suits a self-taught starter. No stipend is stated and public engineering evidence is thin.

companies.name: Jubilant FoodWorks Bangladesh Ltd.
companies.note: Franchise operator for Domino's Pizza in Bangladesh, running a structured paid trainee programme. Stable and it does invest in juniors, but the IT track is corporate IT support rather than product engineering, so weigh it against a software house if you want to build engineering depth.

companies.name: ShareDeal
companies.note: Early-stage group-buying marketplace connecting customers with farmers and vendors. The stack described is real product work, but BDT 25,000 is low for a two-to-three year developer in Dhaka.

companies.name: T1m9m
companies.note: Small Sylhet outfit with almost no public footprint, working on Envato marketplace products. It does promise senior code review, which is worth something to a junior, but it discloses no pay and the name is hard to verify.

companies.name: Solver/Yilmak Bangladesh
companies.note: Dhaka operation hiring internal IT support. It genuinely opens the door to fresh graduates, but the work is business-application support rather than software engineering, and no pay is disclosed.

companies.name: Yupsis
companies.note: Rajshahi software house that publishes salary bands on every opening and states plainly that it hires on skill rather than academic background. Both are unusually good signs for a fresher; the trade-off is a small public engineering footprint.

companies.name: Care Guide
companies.note: Gulshan services company advertising an internal IT role. It labels the position an internship while asking for two to three years, which is a mislabel worth noting, and it defers pay to expertise. Night shift only.

companies.name: Falaq Digital
companies.note: Dhaka group posting the same .NET and Angular opening under two entity names, Falaq Digital and Falaq Food, which makes the hiring entity ambiguous. No pay is disclosed; confirm which company would employ you.

companies.name: European IT Institute
companies.note: Dhaka IT training institute hiring part-time instructors. Useful for teaching experience and certification exposure, but it is a training provider rather than an engineering employer, so it will not build production experience.

companies.name: Square Textiles Division
companies.note: In-house IT function of a large, long-established Bangladeshi industrial group, so job security and on-time pay are strong. The trade-off is internal business systems work rather than product engineering, and salary is only described as negotiable.

companies.name: ZattWorld Solutions
companies.note: Small Chattogram software house. Its circulars are thin on technical detail and duplicate blocks of text, and pay is only negotiable, so ask for specifics on stack and salary early.

companies.name: iHealthScreen Inc
companies.note: Health-screening software company with a US-registered parent and a Dhaka engineering team. The work is real product development, though the degree requirement is rigid and pay is only negotiable.

companies.name: StudyNet Pty Ltd
companies.note: Australian-owned education technology provider with roughly sixteen years of trading history and partnerships with over twenty-six universities, operating a Dhaka development team. Stable, though salary is only described as negotiable.

companies.name: Kirrhosoft
companies.note: Small Dhaka software company hiring its first dedicated designer alongside backend staff, which suggests an early-stage team. Ownership is broad for a junior, but no pay is disclosed.

companies.name: MIAKI
companies.note: Dhaka digital and telecom value-added services company. The work gives real exposure to operator-scale campaign systems, but no pay is disclosed.

companies.name: TECHNIX TECHNOLOGY
companies.note: Small technology services firm whose LinkedIn listings stay up long after posting, including circulars dated 2023, so verify with the company that any opening is still live. No pay is disclosed.

companies.name: SARLEO
companies.note: Small Dhaka engineering outfit running a structured six-month paid internship with a stated stipend and hybrid hours. Judging candidates on projects rather than experience is a genuinely fresher-friendly signal, though the company itself is hard to verify publicly.

companies.name: ADN Semiconductors
companies.note: Semiconductor design arm of ADN Group, working across IT, telecom and silicon engineering. One of very few places in Bangladesh offering genuine RTL design and verification experience, and it pairs interns with mentors. Pay is not disclosed.

companies.name: Online Creative Network
companies.note: Bangladeshi software and cloud company selling point-of-sale products from Mymensingh. The role is customer support rather than development, so it builds product and client skills more than engineering depth. No pay is disclosed.

companies.name: Avian BPO & IT
companies.note: Dhaka BPO and IT services company. It states a clear monthly salary that is well above the usual entry-level band and does not gate the role behind years of experience, both of which are good signs for a first job.

companies.name: Sheikh Brothers
companies.note: Non-technology business hiring one person to cover both IT support and digital marketing. Pay is stated but low, and the split role means little engineering progression; useful mainly as a first paid IT job.

companies.name: Synesis IT
companies.note: Long-established Dhaka IT services company known for large government and enterprise systems work, including national helpline and digital service projects. A solid place to learn infrastructure under senior engineers, though this circular discloses no stipend.

companies.name: BDGAME STUDIO
companies.note: Small Banani game studio offering Unreal Engine work, which is scarce in Bangladesh. It waives degree requirements for demonstrated skill, but it asks interns to commit to a minimum one-year contract without disclosing any stipend; settle both points before signing.

companies.name: DG Infotech Limited
companies.note: Dhaka IT services company running a broad structured internship that covers architecture, secure coding, DevOps and cloud rather than just coding tasks. Good learning breadth for a first placement; no stipend is disclosed.

companies.name: Envobyte Ltd.
companies.note: Software house with a Khulna office doing mobile product work, which gives a fresher real release-cycle exposure outside Dhaka. It expects a QA hire to guide juniors fairly early and discloses no pay.

companies.name: Canadian International School Dhaka
companies.note: Established international school hiring a Laravel intern for in-house systems. Stable and low-pressure, but it is an education institution rather than a software company, so there is no engineering team to grow into. No stipend disclosed.

companies.name: DNS Group
companies.note: Posts an AI internship with the employment type recorded as volunteer and no stipend named, under a staffing and recruiting industry tag. The LLM work may be worthwhile, but confirm whether anything is paid before starting.

companies.name: Renaissance Group
companies.note: Established Bangladeshi group hiring a trainee for internal IT administration. Stable employer, but the role is asset and vendor management rather than software work, so it will not build engineering skill. No pay disclosed.

companies.name: DBM SOFT LTD.
companies.note: Small Dhaka software company taking interns onto real web projects with developer supervision. Reasonable first placement; no stipend is disclosed, so ask.

companies.name: TikWeb
companies.note: Dhaka software firm offering a short structured QA internship. Fine for a first taste of release testing, though three months is brief and no stipend is disclosed.

companies.name: SariyaHOST
companies.note: Small Narayanganj web hosting provider. The circular in the feed is a recycled 2023 posting asking for certified senior Linux and virtualization skills, so there is no early-career evidence here. Pay is negotiable only.

companies.name: foodpanda Bangladesh
companies.note: Delivery Hero subsidiary and the leading food delivery platform in Bangladesh. Stable and well known, but most Dhaka openings are operations, commercial and customer experience work; engineering sits in the regional hubs. Pay is not stated in circulars.

companies.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
companies.note: UN specialised agency with a long-standing Bangladesh country office. Very stable and it publishes UN salary grades, but it is not an engineering employer; CSE-relevant openings are occasional IT and data support posts on fixed-term service contracts.

companies.name: SEOPAGE1
companies.note: Dhaka digital marketing agency that recruits trainees in bulk through job boards. The work is SEO, content and WordPress rather than software engineering, so it suits a marketing career more than a CSE one. Pay is not stated.
